paper_metadata.title: EAQGA: A Quantum-Enhanced Genetic Algorithm with Novel Entanglement-Aware Crossovers

summary: The paper proposes an Entanglement‑Aware Quantum‑Enhanced Genetic Algorithm (EAQGA) that generates shallow quantum circuits encoding correlations between variables. On simulator experiments with 30‑ and 40‑asset portfolio optimization instances (100 runs each), EAQGA consistently achieved higher fitness than classical GA and AQGA. On IBM’s 127‑qubit ibm_quebec processor with a 100‑asset problem, EAQGA produced average fitness values 33.6% higher than GA and 37.2% higher than AQGA after 20 iterations.

experiments.description: Entanglement-aware quantum genetic algorithm (EAQGA) for binary portfolio optimization, evaluated on simulator across 30-asset and 40-asset subsets with population sizes 10 and 20.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial circuits start in equal superposition via Hadamard gates; population initialized by measuring superposition circuits once

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable; binary portfolio selection x_i in {0,1}
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize mu^T x - q * x^T Sigma x subject to x_i in {0,1}
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary feasibility inherent in basis encoding; no additional penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on randomly selected S&P 500 stock subsets
problem_instance.dataset_name: S&P 500 / Yahoo Finance via Qiskit Finance

dataset_specification.description: 10 non-overlapping random subsets of 30 stocks from S&P 500; historical data from 2023-10-01 to 2024-09-30; daily interval

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical prices converted to returns R_it = P_it/P_i(t-1) - 1; mean returns and covariance matrix computed from historical data; covariance normalized for pair selection
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 subsets; each algorithm run 100 times per subset; average and standard deviation of fitness over 20 iterations reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: GA and AQGA baselines; brute-force optimum for comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Bayesian optimization used to tune hyperparameters on a randomly selected subset
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Fitness evaluation and elitism pool sorting; average and standard deviation computed over repeated runs

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: fitness over iterations; EAQGA improves and stabilizes across runs

speedup_claims.factor: EAQGA achieved the best average fitness across all 30-asset simulator subsets; exact percentage improvement not stated in the table
speedup_claims.conditions: 30-asset subsets, simulator, population sizes 10 and 20, 20 iterations
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports averages over 100 runs per subset; no formal speedup or runtime advantage is claimed.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No asymptotic complexity or speedup analysis provided; experiments only compare heuristic solution quality across GA, AQGA, and EAQGA on simulated circuits with 30 variables.
limiting_factors: Algorithm is a heuristic hybrid workflow dominated by classical GA steps
Low entanglement circuits intentionally designed to remain classically simulable
Evaluation metric is heuristic fitness rather than computational runtime

notes: num_qubits inferred as 30 from the 30-asset subset with 1 qubit per binary variable; paper does not explicitly state qubit count for the simulator runs.
hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper names the Qiskit MPS simulator rather than a real QPU.
No asymptotic speedup order is characterized; paper explicitly states no formal quantum advantage claim.
Paper explicitly states it does not claim formal quantum advantage and that the algorithm can still be simulated efficiently on classical hardware (Section IV‑E).
Results only show improved heuristic fitness relative to classical GA/AQGA implementations.
